newsitem.title: CANADA: Domtar heavily traded on debt redemption.
newsitem.headline: Domtar heavily traded on debt redemption.

text.p: Domtar Inc topped Toronto's actives roster on Thursday, rising in heavy volume on what traders said was hedging activity connected with the redemption of the company's convertible debentures.
"It is assumed to be related to the redemption of their convertible debt," said one U.S. arbitrageur.

But speculation still abounds that the Quebec pulp and paper company could be a takeover prospect in the future. In February, the Quebec government hired ScotiaMcLeod Inc to look for a buyer for its 24 percent stake in the firm.
But Thursday's action was dismissed as debt-related.
"If there had been anything going on (today), you would have seen more price activity," said the arbitrageur.
The stock rose 0.15 to 11.35 in Toronto with 4.27 million shares changing hands, including a 4.21 million share block crossed by Gordon Capital Corp late morning.
Gordon Capital declined to comment on the activity.
In Montreal, the stock gained 0.10 to 11.30 in trade of 1.04 million shares including a one million share block crossed by Nesbitt Burns Inc.
"We don't know exactly why people trade. They don't have to tell us," said Domtar spokesman Denis Couture.

"What we know though is that on the 19th of August, we issued a press release saying that we are redeeming our convertible debentures...While we cannot say for certain that this is what is causing the acitivity, this may have something to do with it," he added.

Domtar on August 19, called C$150 million worth of 8.0 percent convertible unsecured subordinated debentures due March 18, 2003. Holders were given the option of redeeming the debentures at a price equal to 100 percent of their principal amount, payable on September 19 or converting the debt prior to September 18.
-- Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com
